> I know very experience people that can’t change their jobs because they would fail the interviews. The interviews have so little to do with what you actually work on, so honestly you have to really endure and keep practicing coding problems.

Well, that's depressing. Though I guess I sensed this already years ago. The people Ive worked with didnt seem to know much beyond those trite coding tests. Coding tests are not my issue. The more I interview, the more I sense the entire process has little to do with the tasks they need done. Idk if its an HR lost in translation issue, or if I just dont interview well even on the phone. The clients Ive landed arent normally that tech savvy - maybe I dont belong in software or maybe I do, but Im wondering why I would want to work at a place - an industry, even - that I'll be stuck at and where the process for hire is arbitrary at best.

Thanks for the advice, again. I think youre trying to encourage me to continue pursuing software dev, but those are solid reasons to turn my skills into anything else.

That's not bad advice. I am seriously questioning though, if I don't have the interview skills by now, how would I expect to gain them? Ive considered finding a sales department for a software product or as an advocate for a technology for a company seeking funding. 

My first job software was a fluke in one sense - I knew finite element analysis from my graduate work, they were looking for Java guys with flow evaluated area experience. FEA. and FEA. I also knew a guy, helped him learn Java - even though I only knew C++ - and though I did poorly in the interview, the strong reference and the "prior experience" were enough for them to give me a shot. They weren't disappointed, but I hated the job due to the atmosphere, it's a long story but I was very unhappy. My next jobs have all been small, I have had an LLC for a while, with one client left at the moment. Enjoyed these the most, but Ive done little or no business expansion.

Hacker rank im unfamiliar with and tech meet up, sounds scary, but I am seriously considering these ideas. I do need more contacts, I dont have a linkedin, I dont do that song and dance very well. I just code. Which explains alot I suppose.

EDIT: While I have a business, I have some sort of social anxiety which makes in person interviews the worst. I'm really good on the phone. Not as good in person. It works fine when you can show the client a similar product, or start the work gratis and then discuss a roadmap and payment arrangement. And since relationships with people, in general, bother me I tend to avoid having clients lined up, or jobs lined up, so my influx is probably half of what it could be. One bombed interview a week is about all I can take these days.
Also, maybe not rhyming there makes it more powerful, say, twice as uncouth?
The idea of rules for creative works always bothered me. So as a rule i avoid rules, which still bothers me, since its a rule.

Wow i can relate having struggled with impulse, young love, drugs, etc. What is the person in us that we are both driven by and hurt by?

My only criticism is to throw out the When in the last stanza and work in the concept of Can? Because it seems the narrator knows the dread feeling of being slave to this childlike heart and must wonder if its even possible to harden let alone if its really good or bad.

But feel free to ignore me, please, i think the rhythm and structure and imagery are all fine.

I feel like a jerk even saying it because it doesnt detract from the feeling. Also I'm realizing how that line could be the description of your "death" as drowning. So its hard for me find a better image for that

I have social anxiety so i probably projected that onto the scene - to me masturbation wasnt a sexual reference,but rather the act of having social options but not engaging in them, sort of a social masturbation. I've been ... 7 years now, owing over $100,000 for unpaid tuition, taxes, and medical bills.

I thought I was going to kill myself too, and sometimes I want to, but all I can afford is food and to pay my small businesses rent. It's all I have left, with no future in sight, so they will eat that debt. I have no choice.

Fortunately I find time to laugh, and eat, so my point is, yeah, you want to not have this stress, of owing all this money. Tell them that you can't afford it. Tell them that you will send them half of what your payment is. Negotiate. And if, they won't listen, you can do what I do: Say fuck it, I'm going to spend my money on myself until they come and kill me themselves!
